narr: In wake of a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) that moved through the region during the morning hours of July 11th, the air mass remained stable for much of the day, despite a weak surface frontal system becoming stationary across portions of the I-30 corridor of Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas. However, strong insolation throughout the day helped to erode the cloud cover by mid and late afternoon across East Texas, allowing for warming temperatures and air mass recovery. Southwest winds helped to usher increased instability northeast into the area from Central Texas by late afternoon/early evening, with an upper level disturbance rotating east beneath a large upper trough helping to enhance large scale forcing near the stationary surface front and instability axis over East Texas. As a result, showers and thunderstorms containing heavy rainfall continued to develop and move repeatedly over Southern Smith, Northern Cherokee, and Central Rusk Counties during the evening through the early morning hours of July 12th. Widespread rainfall amounts of 3-6 inches fell across this area, with isolated higher amounts between 6-7 inches falling along the Smith/Cherokee County line near the town of Bullard. These excessive rainfall amounts resulted in flash flooding in Northern Cherokee County, where FM 855 north of Highway 175 near the Cuney community was closed due to flooding. ||While these storms eventually diminished during the mid and late morning hours of the 12th, strong heating and increased instability along the weak stationary boundary again resulted in scattered strong to severe thunderstorms during the mid-afternoon across portions of North and Northeast Texas, with these storms tracking east across Kaufman, Northern Van Zandt, and Southern Rains Counties into Wood County. These storms downed a large tree branch across FM 778 just southeast of Quitman, before quickly weakening shortly thereafter as it moved into Western Upshur County.
